faq.q: How much does Justice On Demand charge?
faq.a: Justice On Demand publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Justice On Demand offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Justice On Demand publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock and the firm states it will visit clients in hospital or at home.

faq.q: Where does Justice On Demand have offices?
faq.a: Justice On Demand publishes five offices, among them Mesa, Queen Creek, Gilbert and Chandler. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Justice On Demand?
faq.a: Justice On Demand names four attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: Arizona does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.q: What has Law Firm Listings verified about Justice On Demand?
faq.a: Justice On Demand scores 38 and sits at Verified. Passed: website and footprint. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure, discipline and entity registration. Every row of the scorecard above names where the value came from and when it was read. Nothing on this profile was supplied by the firm for payment, and no placement here can be bought.
